subject.title: Agent declared tools != effective session tools: no strict inheritance mode, no visibility, no clipping reason trace

question: Should OpenClaw add a fail-closed strict tool inheritance mode, or first expand the read-only diagnostics contract for declared/effective/removed tools and structured blocked reasons?
rationale: This changes the operator security boundary for exec, sandbox, provider/runtime, and subagent tool availability, and may add config/API behavior that existing users discover only when a session stops or fails closed.

options.title: Diagnostics-first contract
options.body: Expose declared, effective, removed, and blocked-by metadata through existing read-only surfaces first, then revisit strict fail-closed mode after the upgrade and UX contract is clear.

options.title: Opt-in strict mode now
options.body: Add a new explicit strict config mode that fails fast when runtime clipping changes declared tools, with docs, tests, and doctor/upgrade guidance in the same change.

options.title: Accept current visibility
options.body: Treat `tools.effective` plus audit logs as sufficient and close the strict parity request as not planned.

recommendation.title: Diagnostics-first contract
recommendation.body: Expose declared, effective, removed, and blocked-by metadata through existing read-only surfaces first, then revisit strict fail-closed mode after the upgrade and UX contract is clear.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest recent history across the effective-tools context, policy pipeline, and documented gateway tool method contract.
